t: Maximum Moves to Kill All Pawns: Knight BFS + Bitmask Game DP
o: We restate: a knight starts at (kx,ky); Alice and Bob alternately pick any remaining pawn and teleport-capture it at the cost of the shortest knight distance from the knight's current cell. Alice wants to maximize the total distance, Bob to minimize it. Example 2 shows Alice picking (2,2) first (cost 2) rather than greedily close pawns, because later turns matter more. Constraints (≤15 pawns, 50×50 board) scream bitmask DP over pawn subsets, with all-pairs shortest knight distances precomputed by BFS.
k: Precompute pairwise shortest knight distances with 16 BFS runs (from the start cell and each pawn) — the board and pawns are static.
The game state is (set of captured pawns, knight's current pawn); whose turn it is is determined by the popcount of the mask.
Alice maximizes and Bob minimizes at alternating layers of the subset-DP — a classic minimax over 2^n · n states.

a.n: Approach 1: All-pairs BFS + Bitmask Minimax DP
a.i: Since only relative distances between the 16 relevant cells matter, run one BFS per relevant source cell on the 50×50 grid. Then dp[mask][i] = best total moves accumulated when the captured set is `mask`, the last captured pawn is `i`, and the knight sits on pawn i. Expanding mask → mask|2^k costs dist(i,k); the player who makes that move is Alice iff popcount(mask) is even (she moved first), so we apply max or min accordingly.
s: Map pawns to indices 1..n with the knight start as index 0; BFS from each of the m=n+1 cells to fill dist[m][m].
Initialize dp[1<<i][i] = dist(0, i+1) for each first capture.
Process masks in increasing order; for each state, relax dp[mask|2^k][k] with dp[mask][i] + dist(i,k), taking max when popcount(mask) is even (Alice's move) and min otherwise.
a.t: O(16 · 2500 + 2^n · n² ) — 16 BFS sweeps over the 50×50 board, then the subset DP with n transitions per state
a.sp: O(2^n · n + m²) for the DP table and distance matrix

w: This is the intended solution; there is no meaningfully faster family of algorithms since the game itself lives on subsets. Pitfalls: forgetting that the knight passes through pawns freely (BFS ignores pawns entirely), mixing up whose turn it is (popcount parity of the mask *before* the move), and initializing the max-layer incorrectly (use a sentinel and treat unreachable as −∞ for Alice, +∞ for Bob). Follow-ups: what if pawns block the knight (then BFS must treat pawns as obstacles and distances change per mask), or if the board were larger (distance oracle via formula instead of BFS).
